stem: What makes a shift handoff decision-ready?
choices: List every unfinished task so the next shift can decide priority independently.
State priority, affected identity/scope, current evidence, completed actions, dependencies, unresolved decision, due timing, and the role that owns the next decision.
Provide only the leading diagnosis or interpretation so the handoff stays concise.
Report only completed work and leave open issues in the source system.
rationale: A decision-ready handoff must tell the next shift what matters most, what is affected, what is known, what has already been done, what remains unresolved, and who owns the next decision. A flat task list forces the receiving shift to reconstruct priority, while diagnosis-only or completed-work-only handoffs can hide dependencies and urgent open risks.
